Summary: Mainframe to Salesforce Revenue Cloud Migration - Membership Renewal & Billing Communications
Description:
Retire the 10 legacy COBOL batch programs (ACSC membership renewal / billing / card-decline notification pipeline) and rebuild the equivalent business logic on Salesforce Revenue Cloud - confirmed as native Revenue Lifecycle Management (standard Order/OrderItem/Asset via the revenue_o2aflows package), NOT the CPQ/Billing (SBQQ/blng) managed packages originally assumed.

Source system inventory and legacy behavior: docs/cobol-legacy/README.md
Target architecture: docs/salesforce-design/high-level-design.md
Real org schema (field-verified audit): docs/salesforce-design/data-dictionary-reference.md
Real outbound delivery pipeline (AFT/MOVEit job config): docs/salesforce-design/moveit-aft-reference.md
Process flows: docs/salesforce-design/workflows.md
Apex design scaffold: force-app/main/default/classes/

Scope covers: renewal SMS/push eligibility notifications (MD021EX, MD022 family), billing email (MD134ML), card-decline/dunning email (MD572EM), and EFT reject / bill-plan reconciliation (MD058CB). Members are Person Accounts in the real org, not a separate Contact.

Summary: Design Revenue Cloud Target Architecture & Data Model
Description:
Design the target Salesforce Revenue Cloud object model, integration architecture, and Apex class inventory that replaces the legacy DB2 tables and file-based batch pipeline.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Object-model mapping table (legacy DB2/COBOL concept -> Revenue Cloud object) corrected against a real, field-verified org audit (done - see data-dictionary-reference.md) and reviewed/signed off by a Salesforce architect
- Person Account confirmed as the real member model (done) - Asset.AccountId points directly at the Person Account, not a separate Contact
- Billing/Payment data source identified - genuinely unresolved, see the new 'Resolve Billing/Payment Data Source' story
- Renewal modeling approach (Order amendment vs. Asset field update) confirmed with the business
- Asset -> campaign-code lineage gap resolved (Asset does not currently carry a campaign-code identifier forward from the Order/OrderItem)

Status note: corrected against the real org's field-verified data dictionary (docs/salesforce-design/data-dictionary-reference.md) - the original CPQ/Billing (SBQQ/blng) assumption was wrong and has been replaced throughout. Membership-number generation (the MD999CK replacement) is confirmed already implemented in the org (RVNMembershipNo Apex) - remaining gap there is a 53%-blank data backfill, not a design gap. Campaign_Code__c/Campaign_Action__c exist as real objects but have zero automation today.

No Invoice/Payment/BillingAccount object of any kind appears in the real org's field-verified data dictionary (7 objects audited: Order, OrderItem, Asset, Account, Person Account, Campaign_Code__c, Campaign_Action__c). This blocks the amount-due (MD610BR-equivalent) and payment-in-transit (FN435BT-equivalent) logic in the renewal batch and the card-decline trigger source for the dunning handler.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Confirm whether a Billing/Payment object exists elsewhere in the org outside this audit's scope, or needs to be built
- If it exists: document its real fields the same way data-dictionary-reference.md does for the audited objects
- If it doesn't: decide the source of truth for amount-due and payment-in-transit before RenewalEligibilityRules.hasPaymentInTransit()/matchesBillingEventFilter() and CardDeclineDunningHandler's trigger source can be finalized
- All current blng__Payment__c/blng__Invoice__c references in the Apex scaffold are explicitly flagged placeholders, not assumed real - do not re-guess a different object/field name without this confirmation

Status note: new - split out from the architecture story because this single gap blocks acceptance criteria on two other stories (Renewal Batch, Card-Decline Handler) and deserves its own owner/timeline.

Real Control-M/AFT job configuration (docs/salesforce-design/moveit-aft-reference.md) shows the actual delivery pipeline is two-stage: a plaintext file lands in local staging (Stage 1, mainframe-local), then a Stage 2 encryption step PGP-encrypts it and forwards it onward. User-confirmed 2026-09-01: MOVEit itself is capable of PGP encryption, so Stage 2 is plausibly MOVEit's own automation running the PUB_SalesForce-keyed task, not a separate non-MOVEit system - the leading integration candidate is now Apex uploading a plaintext file directly to a MOVEit-exposed HTTPS endpoint, with MOVEit's own automation applying encryption and forwarding on (very plausibly to SFMC, based on the PGP key naming and SFMC MobileConnect-specific column terminology in the real SMS extract).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Confirm with the MOVEit/AFT team the specific HTTPS endpoint/API Salesforce should call to hand off a plaintext file, and what auth/credential it needs
- Confirm whether a new MOVEit task/folder needs provisioning for Salesforce-originated files, or whether the existing PUB_SalesForce task/path can be reused as-is
- Confirm whether the final consumer past MOVEit is in fact Salesforce Marketing Cloud (strongly indicated, not yet certain)
- Replace NotificationGatewayService's placeholder MOVEIT_NAMED_CREDENTIAL/MOVEIT_UPLOAD_PATH with the real, confirmed endpoint once known
- Confirm whether the downstream import (if SFMC) is header-mapped or positional, since column order matters for a positional import

Status note: narrowed from a fully-open transport question to a specific endpoint/credential/provisioning question now that MOVEit's own encryption capability is confirmed. Still blocks final implementation of NotificationGatewayService.flush().

Legacy and target both deliver SMS/Push/Email content as a file, not a live API call: accumulate rows across a batch run into an in-memory extract per channel, then generate ONE file per channel per run in the real, sample-confirmed column layout, ready to hand off to the existing AFT/MOVEit pipeline (see 'Confirm Apex-to-AFT Pipeline Hand-off Mechanism' for the still-open transport question).

Acceptance Criteria:
- NotificationGatewayService accumulates per-channel records across a batch run (queueSms/queuePush/queueEmail) and flushes one file per channel per run, instead of one callout per message - done
- Real column layouts adopted for SMS/Push (9 columns), Email (11 columns), and MD058CB's CAU email sub-format (8 columns, semicolon-delimited and space-padded) - done, see SMS_PUSH_COLUMNS/EMAIL_COLUMNS/CAU_EMAIL_COLUMNS in NotificationGatewayService.cls
- Remaining gaps closed: MD058CB's SMS/Push channels (no real sample yet) and full MD022* fixed-width PIC X(nnn) layout if it differs from the now-confirmed CSV shape
- PGP encryption confirmed OUT OF SCOPE for this class - it already happens outside Salesforce in the existing Stage 2 AFT job (done, do not re-add it here)
- Governor-limit review updated to reflect batched file uploads instead of per-message callouts - done

Status note: file-generation logic is in good shape; what remains is the transport hand-off, tracked separately in 'Confirm Apex-to-AFT Pipeline Hand-off Mechanism'.

Summary: Build EFT Reject / Bill-Plan Reconciliation Batch (EftReconciliationBatch)
Description:
Replace MD058CB: reconcile EFT card-auto-update rejects against household bill-plan status, generating out-of-sync/out-of-territory correspondence and SMS/Push/Email notifications.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Eft_Cau_Reject__c staging object defined for inbound EFT reject records
- EftReconciliationBatch deployed, covering the bill-plan/out-of-territory/days-to-expiration branches
- Out-of-territory check uses the real Account.Out_Of_Territory__c field (done) - replaces an originally guessed lodge-code list
- CAU email output uses the real, sample-confirmed layout (done); SMS/Push channels for this program remain an unconfirmed fixed-width gap
- Explicit business decision recorded on the dormant bill-plan-flip-to-AM logic (currently disabled in production since MEM-480905) - confirm permanently retired before finalizing
- Retry/checkpoint semantics validated against actual at-least-once vs. exactly-once processing requirements (legacy program has GO TO-based deadlock retry with no direct Apex equivalent)
- Parity-tested against legacy MD058CB output for a full semi-monthly cycle

Status note: design scaffold exists (force-app/main/default/classes/EftReconciliationBatch.cls) and corrected against the real data model - the largest and highest-risk program in scope (2,200+ lines of source).

Summary: Parallel Run & Validation Against Legacy Output
Description:
Run each migrated wave side by side with its legacy COBOL equivalent for at least one full billing/renewal cycle, diffing output before treating Salesforce as authoritative.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Diff process defined comparing legacy flat-file extracts to Salesforce Correspondence_Log__c records / generated files, per wave
- Sign-off obtained per program family before cutover
- Data-quality edge cases the legacy code already handles (e.g. all-zero phone numbers, missing country codes) confirmed as carried over correctly
- Known real-org data-quality gaps accounted for, not assumed clean: Asset.Status null on 97% of Assets, Asset.CLUB_CODE__c never fires (use Club__c instead), Asset.Member_Number__c 53% blank

Switch the notification pickup to source from the Salesforce-generated extracts feeding into the existing AFT/MOVEit pipeline, retire the corresponding JCL schedule per program, and keep each COBOL program dormant for one full cycle before removal.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Salesforce-generated extracts confirmed compatible with the existing Stage 2 encrypt/transfer job's expected input, with no format changes required (or format changes coordinated in advance)
- JCL schedule retired per program family only after its parallel-run sign-off
- Rollback plan documented in case a retired program needs to be reactivated during the dormancy period
